text:
Possibly, but it isn't confirmed yet.

Hansen/UMD maps about 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025 on this 345.6 ha property (3.9% of its area). Other sources suggest the affected area was mostly native forest:
- JRC shows 98% of the loss area was forest in 2020.
- MGAP's 2021 map classifies about 13.1 ha as native forest, 0.4 ha as outside mapped forest, and none as planted forest.

The assessment is pending corroboration. 2025 is the latest year in the series, so there is no later year to show whether the loss is persistent.

The evidence also does not show:
- whether this was deforestation or a land-use change, since Hansen loss includes any stand replacement;
- the cause (harvest, fire, storm, clearing);
- whether it was legal or authorized;
- who is responsible.

Treat it as a probable native-forest loss candidate that needs follow-up with later-year data.
